title: A Producer Just Tore Up Salman Khan's Legal Notice on Camera. Now Salman's Ex-Girlfriend Is Backing Him.
excerpt: Amit Jani, the producer of Kala Hiran — a film inspired by the 1998 blackbuck poaching case — says he received death threats from fan armies within 36 hours of the announcement. He responded by ripping the notice apart on video and challenging them to send whoever they want.
body:
The announcement of *Kala Hiran: The Battle for Legacy* was always going to be provocative. A courtroom crime thriller inspired by a high-profile poaching case that has followed Bollywood's biggest star for nearly three decades — the makers had to know what was coming. What they may not have anticipated was the speed and ferocity of the response.

Within days of the poster's release, Salman Khan's legal team dispatched a formal notice to the film's casting director, Akshay Pandey. The notice alleged a "gross violation of personality rights" and demanded the immediate removal of all promotional material. Khan's lawyers argued that since the 1998 blackbuck case is still pending before the Rajasthan High Court on appeal, any dramatisation of the events constitutes prejudicial content that could influence an unresolved judicial matter. The notice demanded a complete halt to both production and promotional activity.

## Then Came the Threats

Producer Amit Jani says the legal notice was the civil part. In a video that has since gone viral, Jani disclosed that within 36 hours of the film's announcement, he received over a thousand messages — abusive language, threats, and warnings about his safety if he returned to Mumbai. He traced the hostility to fan communities in Dharavi, Dongri, and Jogeshwari. The situation escalated when Jani received a message purportedly from D-Company, a notorious criminal organisation, threatening to "eliminate" his entire family. He acknowledged he could not confirm its authenticity but called it part of a broader intimidation strategy.

Jani's response was not diplomatic. He went on Facebook, posted the legal notice in full, and quoted poet Rahat Indori's famous sher: *"Hai uski aadat dara raha hai"* — loosely translated as, "It is merely his habit to intimidate." Then he released a video in which he tore the notice apart on camera. "Your notice? This is my answer to your notice," he said, before throwing the pieces. "As far as your threats are concerned — the toolkits that threaten you, the gangs that threaten you, the ill-mannered fans — send whoever you want. We will see."

## Somy Ali Enters the Arena

The controversy gained a new dimension when Somy Ali — Salman Khan's former girlfriend and one of his most persistent public critics — publicly backed the producer. Responding to Jani's video, she wrote: "Aapko pura haq hai koi bhi subject pe film banane ka. Sirf guilty log chupte hain aur dhamki dete hai." Translation: "You have every right to make a film on any subject. Only the guilty hide and issue threats."

Jani acknowledged her support immediately, posting: "Thanks for open support."

## The Personality Rights Debate

Beyond the dramatic confrontation, the case has reignited a legal question that Bollywood has been grappling with for years: where do personality rights end and creative freedom begin? Salman Khan's lawyers argue that the film uses his name, image, and events linked to him without consent, and that releasing it while the case is still sub judice could prejudice proceedings. Jani insists *Kala Hiran* is about the Bishnoi community's fight for animal conservation, not a Salman Khan biopic.

Indian courts have been increasingly active on personality rights in recent months. The Delhi High Court has granted similar relief to Naga Chaitanya, Bhuvan Bam, and Sri Sri Ravi Shankar against AI-generated and deepfake content. But a film — even one inspired by real events — occupies a different legal territory than a deepfake advertisement.

## What This Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs who follow Bollywood's power dynamics, this story is a revealing window into how star influence operates off-screen. The speed at which fan armies mobilised, the invocation of organised crime, and the legal machinery deployed within days of a poster release — it says something about the ecosystem that surrounds Bollywood's biggest names.

Whether *Kala Hiran* ever makes it to a screen remains to be seen. But Amit Jani's torn-up legal notice is already the most talked-about promotional moment of the month — which may have been the point all along.

*Sources: Bollywood Hungama, Zoom TV, The Indian Eye, Inshorts*
